participants.note: ACKed; agreed with the author against introducing time type aliases
Tested ACK; suggested follow-up cleanups in peerman_tests
ACKed with non-blocking concerns regarding NodeClock::epoch usage and undocumented behavior changes from increased time precision
Approach ACK and ACK; raised a non-blocking concern preferring std::optional over time_point::min/max sentinels

claims.harm: Expanding uses of the nonstandard NodeClock::epoch constant encourages bad code unnecessarily tied to the unix epoch and promotes magic-constant sentinels
claims.quote: This change seems kludgy and would seem to encourage writing bad code.
claims.settled_by_quote: Code review ACK fab4bd7f2bf8eb78efff00a6d1abcb28187e0063. Changes since last review: tweaking `epoch` comment and commit message as suggested

claims.harm: Switching from second to nanosecond precision can alter comparison outcomes (e.g., peer eviction and block announcement tie-breaking), potentially exposing new corner cases without being documented
claims.quote: Changing behavior should be ok and probably even an improvement, but commit message should clarify whether it is changing or not.

claims.harm: Relying on time_point::min and time_point::max sentinels creates nonsensical time values and obscures semantic states compared to std::optional
claims.quote: I find relying on sentinels (`if (State(staller)->m_stalling_since == NodeClock::time_point::max())`) to be an antipattern, and would have found it more clear if this were a `std::optional`.
claims.settled_by_quote: I'm happy to keep it as-is, it's not a regression vs master and the PR has too many other benefits to be spending too much time/energy on this rather small issue.

support.reason: NodeClock::time_point is an improvement over using integer or duration types to represent time points.
IMO, this is much improved since the last version, and the last version was already a nice cleanup
improved type safety in time handling, this makes the code easier to read and harder to make mistakes.
Nice improvement using the time point type to represent times, instead of duration types or integers.

Code review ACK fab4bd7f2bf8eb78efff00a6d1abcb28187e0063. Changes since last review: tweaking `epoch` comment and commit message as suggested, replacing nPowTargetSpacing with PowTargetSpacing a few places, simplifying HEADERS_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_PER_HEADER calculation making it slightly less precise but off by 1ms at most
Built and ran the unit suites and the p2p functional tests.

result.notes: First read of PR 35315. All non-blocking concerns regarding NodeClock::epoch usage, sentinel values vs std::optional, and behavior changes from increased time precision were resolved through code refactorings, commit message documentation, and reviewer concurrence.
